title: Year of the Rabbit: Personality, Love, Career & Compatibility
intro: Known for their gentle demeanor, quiet elegance, and sharp intuition, those born in the Year of the Rabbit navigate life with grace. Whether you are a Rabbit yourself (born in 1939, 1951, 1963, 1975, 1987, 1999, 2011, or 2023) or simply enchanted by one, this guide unlocks the secrets of the fourth sign in the Chinese zodiac.
personality: Rabbits are the diplomats of the Chinese zodiac, possessing a rare blend of sensitivity, artistic flair, and deep empathy. People born under this sign abhor conflict and will go to great lengths to maintain peace and harmony in their environments. They are naturally cautious and thoughtful, preferring to observe situations thoroughly before taking action. This makes them exceptionally wise and prudent decision-makers. Beneath their calm and sometimes timid exterior lies a resilient core of inner strength and sharp intellect. Rabbits appreciate the finer things in life, often curating beautiful, serene living spaces that reflect their refined tastes. They cherish close friendships and deeply value loyalty, making them trustworthy confidants who are always ready with a comforting word and a listening ear.
love: In romance, Rabbits are deeply devoted, romantic, and fiercely loyal partners. Because they crave emotional security, they take their time finding the right match, preferring a steady, meaningful courtship over casual dating. Once committed, a Rabbit brings immense warmth, tenderness, and attentiveness to the relationship. They can be sensitive to criticism, so they thrive with partners who are gentle, reassuring, and verbally appreciative of their efforts.
career: In the workplace, Rabbits excel in roles that require diplomacy, creativity, and attention to detail. They are not typically drawn to aggressive, high-risk corporate ladders; instead, they shine in careers involving art, design, counseling, law, public relations, and literature. Their natural ability to read people and mediate disputes makes them exceptional team players and respected managers.

faq.ans: The Rabbit is associated with the Wood element in traditional Chinese five-element theory.

faq.q: What is the Rabbit's compatibility with other signs?
faq.ans: Rabbits are most compatible with the Pig, Dog, and Goat, sharing strong mutual understanding and peaceful vibes.
